subject: biology-1
question: A red blood cell is placed in a beaker of pure water. Which statement best predicts what will happen to the cell, based on **osmosis** and tonicity?

options.text: The cell shrinks because water leaves the cell to dilute the beaker.
The cell swells and may burst because water enters by osmosis, moving from the higher water concentration outside to the lower concentration inside.
The cell stays the same size because the membrane stops water movement in both directions.
The cell shrinks because salts leak out of the cell into the pure water.

explanation: Pure water is hypotonic relative to the cell interior, so osmosis moves water from the higher water concentration outside to the lower concentration inside, swelling the cell until it may burst. A has the gradient reversed, since water leaves cells in hypertonic conditions. C ignores that the membrane is permeable to water, and D confuses the moving species, because water moves and salts do not leak here.
